name: NGC 4650A
host_tracer: stars (CaII triplet / Mg absorption, long slit)
host_ref: Sackett+1994 ApJ 436,629 Tab.2; Whitmore+1987; Swaters&Rubin 2003; Coccato+2006 ApJ 643,200; Iodice+2015 MUSE 2D
ring_V_kms: 105-125 deprojected HI at 90 arcsec; 100-120 (MUSE gas at 75 arcsec); HI dV20 = 235
ring_extent: 0-90 arcsec HI (~16 kpc gas, ~50 kpc HI); MUSE to 75 arcsec = 16 kpc
ring_ref: Arnaboldi+1997 AJ 113,585 (ATCA HI); Nicholson 1989 (FP Halpha); Swaters&Rubin 2003 ApJ 587,L23; Iodice+2015 A&A 583,A48
angle_method: difference of photometric/kinematic PAs, MUSE (Iodice+2015: HG 67+/-2, polar disk 160)
baryonic_photometry: YES - full 4-component baryonic decomposition (iodice2015_table1_NGC4650A_mass_model.tsv); M_Kn=-21.37, M_B=-18.67 (Iodice+2003); JHKn imaging
notes: THE reference two-plane system. Both planes have extended rotation; the host-plane curve is the only one in this lane tabulated numerically for a classical PRG.

name: NGC 4262
ring_V_kms: V85/2 = 176 (edge-on, unresolved FAST); resolved HI curve in Khoperskov+14 Fig.3
angle_method: deprojection of the two photometric components (two-fold degenerate); Buson+2011 favour the polar (~90) solution
baryonic_photometry: YES - khoperskov2014_table2_SPRC7_NGC4262_photometry.tsv (disc+bulge masses and scales); V_T=11.46, NUV=16.12, logM_HI=8.6, logM*=10.06 (Akhil+2025 PASA 42,e056)
notes: Only galaxy other than the Milky Way for which a RADIALLY VARYING halo axis ratio was claimed (c/a ~ 0.4 inside, 1.5-2.3 outside).

name: SPRC-7
host_V_kms: circular velocity up to ~300 in the model reconstruction
ring_tracer: ionized gas Hbeta (scanning Fabry-Perot velocity field, tilted-ring)
baryonic_photometry: YES - khoperskov2014_table2 (disc+bulge masses and scales); SDSS ugriz; CO(1-0)/(2-1) upper limits M(H2)<=5.3e9 (Combes+2013)
notes: Largest kinematically confirmed PRG ring (~50 kpc diameter). Halo flattened toward the polar plane: c/a = 1.5+/-0.2 (NFW), 1.7+/-0.2 (isothermal).

name: SPRC-260
baryonic_photometry: partial - SDSS ugriz; logM_HI=10.1, logM*=10.3 (Yu+2026)
notes: Triaxial halo reported: c/b = 0.95, a/b = 1.1 (Moiseev+2014).

name: NGC 4632
host_curve: CURVE (figure only; model released as figure panels)
ring_tracer: HI anomalous/polar gas (MCGSuite single polar ring, grid search in beta, v_rot, Sigma)
angle_method: beta = ring angle to the approaching side of the host in galaxy-plane coords; the models IMPOSE i_r,g = 90
baryonic_photometry: YES - logM_HI=9.37+/-0.01 total (9.1 body / 9.0 anomalous), logM*=9.69+/-0.08 (WISE), SFR=0.73+/-0.07
notes: First PRG found FROM the HI rather than from stellar morphology. Both components resolved in the same cube; ~50% of the HI is in the anomalous component. Authors are explicit that a strong warp is not excluded, hence 'potential' PRG.

name: NGC 6156
notes: Authors flag that the low ring velocity relative to the host's outermost rotation point questions dynamical stability, and that a warped disk may fit better; warped models did not converge.

name: A0136-0801
host_curve: CURVE (figure only, in the cited papers)
host_ref: Schweizer, Whitmore & Rubin 1983 AJ 88,909; Whitmore+1987 ApJ 314,439
ring_tracer: ionized gas Halpha (2-D scanning Fabry-Perot velocity field, >2000 pixels)
ring_V_kms: HI dV20 = 365; V85/2 = 259 +/- 38 at i=40 (unresolved FAST)
ring_extent: polar ring extends to >12 disk scale heights above the host plane; ring reaches ~40 arcsec in H band
ring_ref: Sackett & Sparke 1994 (ASP Conf. 'Astrophysical Discs'); van Gorkom+1987; Cox 1996
angle_method: ring is 'nearly perpendicular' (PRC category A); no numeric inter-plane angle located in the acquired sources
baryonic_photometry: YES - M_B=-19.23 (Iodice+2003); CASPIR H-band + 2MASS JHKs; M_HI = 1.6e9 Msun (Cox 1996); H-band 2-component 2D fit (Iodice+2002a A&A 391,103)
notes: Halo axis ratio q = c/a ~ 0.5 from fitting closed polar orbits to the 2-D Halpha field; spherical halos excluded. The full analysis (Sackett & Pogge 1995) was announced but no refereed version was located.

name: UGC 7576
ring_V_kms: HI dV20 = 465; V85/2 = 284 +/- 34 at i=48 (unresolved FAST)
baryonic_photometry: partial - M_B=-19.02 (Iodice+2003); logM_HI=9.8, logM*=10.4 (Yu+2026); chemical abundances in Spavone+2011
notes: One of the two systems in which Reshetnikov & Combes 1994 measured TWO PERPENDICULAR rotation curves (host stars + ring HI) and inferred dark mass = 1.6x the luminous mass inside 17 kpc. NOT ON arXiv AND NOT IN VIZIER - see REPORT.

name: UGC 9796
ring_V_kms: HI dV20 = 355; V85/2 = 164 +/- 16 at i=53 (unresolved FAST)
baryonic_photometry: partial - M_B=-18.25 (Iodice+2003); logM_HI=10.0, logM*=10.1 (Yu+2026); chemical abundances in Spavone+2011
notes: Second Reshetnikov & Combes 1994 system: dark mass = 3x the luminous mass inside 21.4 kpc. NOT ON arXiv AND NOT IN VIZIER.

name: NGC 2685
ring_V_kms: V_rot 131-184 across the fit; V_t = 147 +/- 15 at 31 kpc
ring_curve: FULL CURVE, TABULATED (21 rings, with per-ring inclination, PA and 3-D spin normal)
angle_method: 3-D tilted-ring fit; PA swings ~125 deg between r=0.9 and r>7 kpc
baryonic_photometry: YES - josza2009_table1_NGC2685_properties.tsv: m_B=12.05, m_I=9.90, M_B=-19.1, M_I=-21.4, L_B=7.0e9, L_I=15.2e9 Lsun, M_HI=1.7e9 Msun, R25=10.8 kpc, R_HI=14.8 kpc
notes: DEMOTED FROM 'CLASSICAL PRG': Jozsa+2009 conclude NGC 2685 is NOT a classical polar ring but ONE extremely warped, kinematically coherent HI disk, inclined ~70 deg to the lenticular body inside and coplanar with it outside. For the programme it is nevertheless the single richest DIRECTION SCAN: V_rot tabulated against a continuously changing orbit-plane orientation inside one baryonic system.

name: NGC 7625
host_tracer: ionized gas + stars (scanning Fabry-Perot + long slit)
ring_tracer: ionized gas (warped polar ring, tilted-ring of the FP field)
angle_method: tilted-ring decomposition of the FP velocity field
baryonic_photometry: partial - logM_HI=9.4, logM*=10.1, NUV-r=3.5 (Yu+2026)
notes: Moiseev 2008 fits radial runs of circular velocity, PA and inclination to the FP field (his Fig. 'Radial variations of kinematic parameters'), i.e. a direction scan like NGC 2685 but warped rather than two clean planes.

name: SPRC-10
baryonic_photometry: partial - SDSS ugriz; logM_HI<=9.0, logM*=10.3 (Yu+2026); in MaNGA
notes: Textbook two-slit confirmation: at PA=39 the gas has a strong LOS gradient while the stars are flat; at PA=138 the reverse. Stars of the ring itself detected beyond r ~ 3-4 arcsec.

name: SPRC-14
baryonic_photometry: partial - SDSS ugriz; CO(1-0)+CO(2-1) DETECTED, M(H2)=8.4e9, M*=23e9 Msun (Combes+2013); logM_HI<=9.0 (Yu+2026)
notes: Ring is significantly curved: near-nuclear counter-rotation relative to the outer ring along PA=130. One of only 5 PRGs with a CO detection.

name: SPRC-69
baryonic_photometry: partial - SDSS ugriz; CO DETECTED M(H2)=4.5e9, M*=11e9 Msun (Combes+2013); logM_HI=9.8 (Yu+2026)
notes: FAST inclination is only 10 +/- 18 deg so the tabulated Yu+2026 V_rot = 1127 +/- 1871 km/s is meaningless; use V_rot,i=90 = 214 +/- 13.

name: SPRC-178
baryonic_photometry: partial - SDSS ugriz
notes: Two-slit observation in Moiseev+2011; NOT among the 40 kinematically confirmed PRGs of Yu+2026, i.e. the polar nature was not confirmed.

name: NGC 660
host_tracer: stars / gas of the host spiral
ring_V_kms: HI dV20 = 325; V85/2 = 150 +/- 10 at i=67 (unresolved FAST)
angle_method: the ring is HIGHLY INCLINED rather than truly polar (Whitmore+1990; Combes+1992)
baryonic_photometry: partial - M_B=-18.25 (Iodice+2003); logM_HI=9.7, logM*=10.0 (Yu+2026); star-forming complexes in Smirnova+2017
notes: Late-type (SB(s)a pec) host, not an S0. Deg+2023 note explicitly that its ring is not perpendicular.

name: AM 2020-504
ring_tracer: ionized gas Hbeta/[OIII]/Halpha, long slit along the ring major axis
ring_V_kms: N-S halves differ by ~60 km/s (within errors); HI dV20 = 182 (flagged UNCERTAIN by van Driel+2002)
baryonic_photometry: YES - M_Kn=-22.63, M_B=-19.60 (Iodice+2003); JHKn CASPIR imaging + 2D light decomposition (Iodice+2002a)
notes: Ring is warped (Arnaboldi+1993). Reshetnikov 2004 replaced the unreliable HI width with the OPTICAL ring V_max from the PRC for this object.

name: NGC 4111
ring_tracer: ionized gas (SAURON IFU, modelled as a superposition of an equatorial and a polar disk)
angle_method: two-component model of the SAURON gas velocity dispersion map
baryonic_photometry: partial
notes: IFU two-plane decomposition, but the two-component nature is inferred from the sigma map rather than from two independently resolved rotators. NOT among the 40 confirmed PRGs of Yu+2026.

name: ESO 415-G26
baryonic_photometry: YES - M_Kn=-22.69, M_B=-19.24 (Iodice+2003); JHKn CASPIR + 2D bulge+disk fit (Iodice+2002a)
notes: Short-ring PRG. Host-plane stellar rotation exists (Whitmore+1987) but the polar plane has only an unresolved HI linewidth in the sources acquired here. CROSS-ID VERIFIED AGAINST NED: the designation MCG-05-07-001 resolves to THIS object (two independent NED objsearch queries returned byte-identical rows at 37.08376, -31.88100). The Khoperskov+2014 halo-shape roster lists ESO 415-G26 and MCG-5-7-1 as SEPARATE entries with different references, so that roster most likely double-counts one galaxy and contains 20 distinct systems rather than 21 -- stated as an inference, since MCG-5-7-1 there could instead be a mistyped designation for a different object.

name: Arp 230
host_curve: not located in the acquired sources
baryonic_photometry: YES - M_Kn=-20.95, M_B=-18.40 (Iodice+2003); JHKn CASPIR
notes: Kinematic confirmation reference in Yu+2026 is Schiminovich+2013 (resolved HI); a two-plane decomposition was not located in the acquired sources.

name: IC 1689
ring_V_kms: HI dV20 = 300 (van Gorkom+1987); FAST NON-DETECTION, logM_HI <= 8.4
baryonic_photometry: partial - M_B=-20.40 (Iodice+2003); logM*=10.4, NUV-r=4.7 (Yu+2026)
notes: FAST did not detect HI (3-sigma upper limit), so the older van Gorkom+1987 dV20 = 300 km/s and the newer limit are in tension; treat the HI velocity with caution.
